Source: Hofstrand (2025b) The largest ethanol markets are located on the East and West coasts of the United States, outside of the primary corn production region. Most ethanol produced in the Midwest and is shipped by mostly commonly by trains and also by barge to other regions. Ethanol is not shipped by pipeline due to fuel properties. Ethanol prices are typically lowest in the Midwest and increase as a function of transportation costs when shipped to other domestic markets. 2.7.3 Coproducts Overview Fuel ethanol coproducts include distillers grains,14 corn gluten meal/feed, corn oil, and carbon dioxide. The gross value of coproducts was $8.4 billion in 2024. Corn grain is approximately two-thirds starch, which is converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide; the remaining is converted into distillers grains and corn oil. Distillers grains are the highest-volume coproduct and are sold as livestock feed, and about one-third is exported to more than 50 countries (Figure 29). The top three export markets in 2024 were Mexico (21%), South Korea (13%), and Indonesia (8%) (RFA 2025b).
